evidence_limit: This review uses timestamped storyboard samples, the full-size poster, the brief, and the structural report—not continuous video or audio. Smooth motion, frame continuity, and listening were not verified. Silence is intentional; the report lists no audio track. The authored fixture is not evidence of shipping-product capabilities.

marks.reason: The premise at 1.58s leads to a design request at 4.75s, a generated page at 6.33s, a warmer revision at 12.67s, and the closing promise at 15.84s. The sampled sequence is coherent.
Chat drives the demonstration: “Design a landing page for an urban garden.” is readable at 4.75s; “Make it warmer.” appears at 9.50s, followed by the peach-and-cream result at 11.09s.
At 1.58s, “Say it.” / “Shape it.” matches the brief exactly. At 15.84s and 17.42s, “Your idea.” / “Already taking shape.” also matches, including punctuation. No spelling errors are evident.

Consistent corner branding, generous margins, restrained typography, and lime underlines establish a deliberate hierarchy. The dark closing card at 15.84s provides strong contrast; the full-size poster preserves clear chat/canvas separation.

The request and refinement are legible in the 4.75s and 9.50s closeups. The canvas headline, illustration, CTA, and lower content remain inside the frame at 12.67s. The full-size poster also shows readable UI without focal clipping.

The same garden page changes from green accents at 6.33s to warmer peach and terracotta at 11.09s and 12.67s. At 14.25s, the interface reunites the conversation and revised canvas, establishing an outcome rather than unrelated slides.
The sampled frames and poster show Forma and the HARVEST demo-page identity, with no recognizable external branding, watermark, personal information, or visibly borrowed footage.

The reported 17.5-second format and sampled premise–request–refinement–result structure make this useful as a launch insert or recording-to-promo example. The outcome and closing message are understandable without narration.

strengths: Clear conversational cause and effect, exact headline copy, and a cohesive cream/ink/lime visual system. The warmer revision is visibly distinguishable, and the final interface overview reconnects the chat with its result.
weaknesses: The main artistic weakness is reduced workspace context: isolated chat crops at 4.75s and 9.50s float in extensive empty space, while canvas-only views hide the application. Retain a slim interface header or context inset to strengthen the software-demo feel. The refinement payoff is also modest—primarily a palette change. A clearer before/after comparison would make that benefit more emphatic without implying additional functionality.
